Most of the analyst's discovery result holds up against the binary, the live server and the crypto. Two findings are new and three claims need fixing.

**Confirmed:**
- Android boot discovery is `GET <HOST3>/dls?PARAM=..&TOKEN=..&SECRET=..`. HOST3 is `"https://"` + `SERVICE_PHP_URL()`, and that function returns `"api-sl.bfww.gumi.sg"` from VA/file offset 0x232711f.
- That string is built with strlen. So overwriting it with `"127.0.0.1:9960"` plus NUL padding is safe. It is the only reference to that literal.
- The response is not authenticated in any way.
- Every value in the response must be a JSON string, because `Json::Value::asCString` @0xf51a2c is just `ldr x0,[x0]; ret`.
- SREE uses AES-128-CBC with key `7410958164354871` and IV `Bfw4encrypedPass`. The client reads padding by taking the last byte, finding its first occurrence with memchr, and zeroing from there.
- The keys the client acts on are `game`, `gumilive`, `resource`, `bgimage`, `force` (only the string `"1"` blocks login) and `force_msg`. `mstv` is ignored because its getter has no PLT caller.
- The PARAM, SECRET and SREE example values reproduce exactly with openssl.
- The live server returns `game="0.0.0.0:9960"`, `mstv` as a string, `force` omitted, and 7 trailing spaces as padding. This confirms the public-host problem and the space-padding problem.

**Corrections:**
1. **SREE size limit.** The base64 is copied with `__memcpy_chk(...,0x200)` into a buffer that was zeroed first. The real limit is therefore 512 base64 characters (after the client strips `\n`), which is at most 384 bytes of ciphertext and at most 383 bytes of inner JSON with PKCS#7. The analyst's figures were 511 characters and about 367 bytes. Anything over 512 characters calls abort(), so the app crashes rather than failing quietly.
2. **Non-2xx behaviour.**
   - `SRM::onNetworkRequestError` returns false (`mov w0,wzr` @0x1c78f20). NetworkManager therefore also puts the request in its retry queue (NM+0x18) and may call the NM+0xa8 delegate, which probably shows an error popup.
   - `parseResponse` still runs on this path, so the SRM map is filled (which affects `PHP_URL` and `RES_URL`), but the NM hosts are not re-initialised.
   - 401/408/503/504 and curl failures are also queued, with no SRM callback.
3. **The `"https://"` literal at 0x2369ce3 has five users, not three.** The two missing ones are `TitleScene::showTermsAndConditions` @0x1b88bb0 and `PusherInterface::initializeCommon` @0x1cde450. All five go through strlen.

**New findings:**
- Exact instruction patches for Option B (switching everything to plain HTTP). The encodings were checked with NDK clang.
- HOST4 (`"https://api-prod-player.bfww.gumi.sg"`, built from `SERVICE_PHP_URL2` at 0x2327133) is never redirected by `/dls`. `TitleScene::updateEvent` calls `retrieveGamePlayer`, which sends `GET HOST4 "/player"`, when the TitleScene state is 9. That literal can be patched the same way.

Other facts that matter for the setup:
- There are no `bf.pem` or `bf.crt` files anywhere in the repo or container. Option A (HTTPS on the server) needs a certificate to be generated.
- The empty string at 0x23270c8 (the NUL that ends `"ios.bfww.gumi.sg"`) is shared by about 60 functions and must never be touched.

- It decrypts to {"game":"0.0.0.0:9960","resource":"0.0.0.0:9960","mstv":"21900","gumilive":"0.0.0.0:9960/","bgimage":"/wallpaper/title_logo20151028.jpg"} followed by 7 spaces of padding.
- ServerCache.cpp:205-222 uses GetDrogonBindHostname() (Drogon.hpp: listeners[0].toIpPort()).
- BfCrypt.cpp:20-46 space-pads (always 1..16 spaces) with NO_PADDING; drogon base64 output has no newlines.
- gumi_live.kdl GameDls declares force as type=bool optional (key "force"), msg as str optional (key "force_msg"), and version as i32::str (key "mstv"). force is never set anywhere in gimuserver.
- deploy/config.docker.json has a single listener 0.0.0.0:9960 with https:false and key/cert "bf.pem"/"bf.crt". Neither file exists in the repo or in the bf-server container (/src).
inferred: Query parameter order is PARAM, TOKEN, SECRET (CCDictionary/uthash keeps insertion order). The hash code itself was not disassembled; the server should not depend on the order.
A non-string JSON value crashes the client. An int or null gives a near-null pointer and strlen faults. An object or array value gives a junk string from the map's memory instead of a crash.

JsonCpp iterates object members in sorted key order (std::map with strcmp). So "FRIEND_ID" and "HANDLE_NAME" come before "SREE", which comes before every lowercase key. With insert-if-absent semantics, a key inside SREE beats the same top-level lowercase key.

Space padding works by luck. With no space in the JSON, memchr finds the start of the padding. Any space in a value (for example force_msg or bgimage) cuts the inner JSON short, the parse fails, and the endpoints silently stay at the Gumi defaults. PKCS#7 is always correct, because compact JSON never contains bytes 0x01-0x10.
"0.0.0.0:9960" as a target address is not usable on the physical phone (and is unreliable even on the emulator). The server needs a configurable public host, "127.0.0.1:9960" when using adb reverse.

With handlingType 0, a TLS or transport failure on /dls produces two retry mechanisms. NetworkManager queues the request (and may show a popup if the NM+0xa8 delegate is set), and SRM::update re-sends every 30 s. Boot never moves past the title screen.

The TitleScene state machine values 7 and 9 (which trigger wallet/query and /player) were not traced, so it is not known whether a normal guest boot ever reaches them. If it reaches /player, the dead HOST4 will stall or fail unless 0x2327133 is patched too.

Option B (all plain HTTP) removes the need for a TLS listener on these code paths, but a TLS-verification patch is still worth applying as a safety net. The name BFCertificateProvider (seen in rodata typeinfo near 0x2319000) suggests custom certificate handling. That belongs to the separate configureCURL/TLS analysis.
unknowns: The exact alphabet Utils::URLEncodedString @0xf2e7ec encodes ('+', '/', '='). This does not matter if the server ignores the query.
What Utils::getBundleName returns at runtime; GCLIENTID is probably "Android_sg.gumi.bravefrontier".

Whether BFCertificateProvider or configureCURL pins certificates in a way that matters for Option A. This is outside the discovery scope.

=== 1. WHAT THE CLIENT SENDS (TitleScene boot) ===
Method: GET, on HOST3.
No API-version path segment is added; that only happens for HOST1.
URL = host[3] + "/dls" + "?" + "PARAM=<urlenc>&TOKEN=<unix>&SECRET=<hex64>"

Headers:
  Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
  Accept:application/json; charset=utf-8
  GCLIENTID: Android_<bundle>
  Content-Length: 0

Parameters:
  TOKEN = decimal time(NULL)
  SECRET = lowercase hex of HMAC-SHA256(key "2398asdflibt19adklk", message TOKEN)
  PARAM = Base64(AES-128-CBC(key "7410958164354871", IV "Bfw4encrypedPass", PKCS7("OS=2&APP_VERSION=1163"[+"&EXTRA_PARAM="+x])))
          Then URL-encoded.

The server may ignore all three parameters. The client checks nothing in the response except the HTTP status and the JSON structure.

Failure behaviour:
- Transport or TLS failure: no callback. NetworkManager queues a retry and SRM re-sends every 30 s, so boot is stuck at the title screen.
- 2xx: parse, then reinitEndPoints, then done.
- 401/408/503/504: queued for retry, no SRM callback.
- Any other non-2xx: parseResponse fills the SRM map, but reinitEndPoints is NOT run (HOST0 and HOST2 stay on Gumi defaults). The request is also queued for retry and may trigger an error popup.
- In short, the server must return 200.

=== 2. libgame.so PATCHES (file offset == VA; check the old bytes before writing) ===

[P1] Discovery host (required). Offset 0x232711f, 20 bytes:
  old 6170692d736c2e626677772e67756d692e736700  "api-sl.bfww.gumi.sg\0"
  new 3132372e302e302e313a39393630000000000000  "127.0.0.1:9960" + 6 NULs
  Safe because the string is built with strlen and this literal has no other reference.

[P2] Optional, recommended: HOST4 (/player). Offset 0x2327133, 29 bytes:
  old "api-prod-player.bfww.gumi.sg\0" = 6170692d70726f642d706c617965722e626677772e67756d692e736700
  new 3132372e302e302e313a39393630 + 15 bytes of 00
  Safe because the string is built with strlen.
  If this is applied, the server also needs GET /player (query gl_id=...). Its response format is not analysed.

DO NOT TOUCH:
  0x23270b8 "ios.bfww.gumi.sg" (length 16 hardcoded in PHP_URL and similar functions)
  0x23270c8 (shared "" used by about 60 functions)
  0x2319e64 "https://api-sl.gl.gumi.sg/" (length 26 hardcoded at 0xf5c0d4 and 0xf5c278)
The /dls response replaces the first and last of these at runtime.

[P3] Scheme: choose ONE of the two options.

Option B (recommended; keeps the server's single plain-HTTP listener). Turn "https://" into "http://" everywhere the boot path needs:
  a) Literal 0x2369ce3, 9 bytes:
       old 68747470733a2f2f00
       new 687474703a2f2f0000
     Affects getPhpUrl, getPhpReidUrl, getChallengeArenaUrl, TitleScene::showTermsAndConditions and PusherInterface::initializeCommon. All use strlen.
  b) GumiLiveManager::init (sets the initial HOST1-HOST4 prefix):
       0xf5fbec: 694ec7f2 -> 49e7c5f2   (movk x9,#0x3a73,lsl32  ->  movk x9,#0x2f3a,lsl32)
       0xf5fbf0: 08028052 -> c8018052   (mov w8,#0x10  ->  mov w8,#0xe, the SSO size byte for 7 characters)
       0xf5fbf4: e9e5e5f2 -> e905e0f2   (movk x9,#0x2f2f,lsl48  ->  movk x9,#0x2f,lsl48)
  c) reinitEndPoints (prefix for "game" -> HOST2 and "gumilive" -> HOST0):
       0x1c7a5c8: 08028052 -> c8018052
       0x1c7a5dc: 684ec7f2 -> 48e7c5f2
       0x1c7a5e0: e8e5e5f2 -> e805e0f2
  Result:
  - /dls goes to http://127.0.0.1:9960/dls.
  - The game PHP base becomes http://<game>/.
  - HOST2 becomes http://<game>.
  - HOST0 becomes http://<gumilive>.
  - Resources stay http://<resource>/content.
  Only adb reverse tcp:9960 tcp:9960 is needed.

Option A (no scheme patches): keep the https:// prefixes.
  - Requires the TLS-verification patch (separate analysis).
  - Requires an HTTPS listener on 9960. bf.pem and bf.crt do NOT exist yet: generate a self-signed pair, put it in the container working directory, and set "https": true.
  - Requires a second "https": false listener (for example 9961) for resources, with resource_host "127.0.0.1:9961", plus adb reverse tcp:9961 tcp:9961.

Then zipalign and apksigner as usual.

=== 3. /dls RESPONSE CONTRACT ===
Status: 200. Content-Type is not checked. The body must be a JSON object whose values are all JSON strings; any number, bool or null crashes the client.

Accepted forms:
  (a) Plain:
      {"game":"127.0.0.1:9960","gumilive":"127.0.0.1:9960/","resource":"127.0.0.1:9960","bgimage":"/wallpaper/title_logo20151028.jpg"}
  (b) Encrypted:
      {"SREE":"<base64 of AES-128-CBC(key 7410958164354871, IV Bfw4encrypedPass, PKCS7(compact inner JSON))>"}
      Limits:
      - Base64 at most 512 characters after any '\n' (more than 512 aborts the client), so the inner JSON is at most 383 bytes.
      - The inner JSON must not contain bytes 0x01-0x10.
      - With non-PKCS7 padding, the pad byte must not occur anywhere in the JSON.
      Verified example (inner JSON {"game":"127.0.0.1:9960","gumilive":"127.0.0.1:9960/","resource":"127.0.0.1:9960","mstv":"21900","bgimage":"/wallpaper/title_logo20151028.jpg"}):
      9SM2eJb+9PwEI868+/7A7WtU+m90mPoQczOewdwtVprLEHYhZjQs+zNJjeIuI7XNtNF4xeLCLFedaYptaL1GPl0752VXoS+LI+gLNRyaNm2dT+JXdLOKTlB7rJ5btCU6C4emy4WT5xE89eouW+LwzJ02sNNdWDYux5d7UJABIPL+V68OPGyaMKdxVZT09rg2

inferred: The complete working redirect is: (client) force the game scheme to http and point the default/bootstrap game host at the local server, AND (server) make the SREE game_ip client-reachable. With both, it works whether or not the Android client ever performs the SREE /dls round-trip: if it skips discovery, map["game"] stays empty and the patched default host 127.0.0.1:9960 is used directly; if it does discovery, the server returns 127.0.0.1:9960 for map["game"]. Either way requests become http://127.0.0.1:9960/bf/gme/action.php.

Because the server is HTTP (https:false), the user's "patch the TLS check" is satisfied by forcing the client scheme https->http; no actual TLS handshake occurs, so cert verification/pinning never runs. The configureCURL VERIFYPEER/VERIFYHOST edits are only a belt-and-suspenders fallback for any residual https request path.

The "0.0.0.0:9960" game_ip from GetDrogonBindHostname() is the specific reason an unmodified decompfrontier server works for the Windows client (WinINet detour ignores the host) but would break an Android client that honors the returned host; this is the 'Android difference' the task asked to find. The bind must stay 0.0.0.0 for Docker port mapping, so game_ip must be set independently (config) rather than by changing the listener address.

Patching the default-host string alone is insufficient because PHP_URL() hardcodes the SSO length to 16; writing a 14-char host leaves 2 bytes of stale content inside the std::string, and c_str() truncation at an embedded NUL would drop the appended path. Hence the paired length-immediate patch (0x20->0x1c) is required so the string is exactly "127.0.0.1:9960".

On the API 36 emulator in its default 4KB page mode and on most current phones (4KB pages), the 4KB-aligned ELF loads fine. On a device actually running 16KB pages, the 4KB p_align would fail to load and cannot be fixed by repackaging alone (needs relinking with max-page-size 16384); this is out of scope for the patch.

Since the modified APK is self-signed with a new key (the original gumi key is unavailable), the existing installed app must be uninstalled first (INSTALL_FAILED_UPDATE_INCOMPATIBLE otherwise). v1+v2 signing suffices (v1 for minSdk16, v2 for API24+; v3 optional).

Keeping native libs DEFLATED (as shipped) is fine and simplest; only 4-byte zipalign is needed. 16KB page alignment (zipalign -P 16) matters only for uncompressed/mmapped libs and is not required here.

=== CLIENT BYTE PATCHES (apply to the extracted arm64-v8a libgame.so) ===

C1 — force main-protocol scheme http (required). Shared "https://" literal.
  file offset 0x2369ce3: original 68 74 74 70 73 3a 2f 2f  ("https://")
                         ->       68 74 74 70 3a 2f 2f 00  ("http://\0")   [8 bytes; following byte 0x2369ceb stays 00]
  Effect: getPhpUrl/getPhpReidUrl/getChallengeArenaUrl/Pusher/T&C now emit http:// (strlen ctor -> "http://").

C2 — point default/bootstrap game host at local server (required). Two edits:
  (a) file offset 0x23270b8: original 69 6f 73 2e 62 66 77 77 2e 67 75 6d 69 2e 73 67 ("ios.bfww.gumi.sg", 16B)
                            ->       31 32 37 2e 30 2e 30 2e 31 3a 39 39 36 30 00 00 ("127.0.0.1:9960\0\0")
  (b) file offset 0x1162e10: original 08 04 80 52 (mov w8,#0x20 -> SSO len 16)
                            ->       88 03 80 52 (mov w8,#0x1c -> SSO len 14)
  Effect: PHP_URL() default becomes exactly std::string("127.0.0.1:9960"); getPhpUrl -> "http://127.0.0.1:9960/".

C3 — NetworkManager/account (GL) host+scheme -> local (apply if guest-login/account uses this subsystem; harmless otherwise):
  file offset 0x2319e64: original "https://api-sl.gl.gumi.sg/" (26B) + 00
                        ->       "http://127.0.0.1:9960/\0" i.e. 68 74 74 70 3a 2f 2f 31 32 37 2e 30 2e 30 2e 31 3a 39 39 36 30 2f 00 (23B); zero-fill remaining bytes up to 0x2319e7e.
  CAVEAT: confirm NetworkManager ctor @0xf5c0d0 uses strlen; if it passes an explicit length (26), also patch that immediate to 22.

C4 (optional, only if any https path survives) — disable cocos CCHttpClient TLS verify in configureCURL:
  file offset 0x102dc5c: 42 00 80 52 (mov w2,#2 VERIFYHOST) -> 02 00 80 52 (mov w2,#0)

=== REPACKAGE + RE-SIGN ===
BT=~/Library/Android/sdk/build-tools/36.1.0
1. Work on a COPY of the APK in a scratch dir. Extract lib/arm64-v8a/libgame.so, apply C1,C2 (and C3 as needed).
2. Replace the entry in the zip (keep it DEFLATED): zip -j (or `jar`/python zipfile) overwrite lib/arm64-v8a/libgame.so.
   Then strip old signature: delete META-INF/CERT.RSA, CERT.SF, MANIFEST.MF.
3. Align (libs compressed -> 4-byte align is sufficient): "$BT/zipalign" -f -p 4 patched.apk aligned.apk
4. Make a keystore once: keytool -genkeypair -keystore bf.keystore -alias bf -keyalg RSA -keysize 2048 -validity 10000 -storepass android -keypass android -dname "CN=bf".
5. Sign v1+v2(+v3): "$BT/apksigner" sign --ks bf.keystore --ks-key-alias bf --ks-pass pass:android --key-pass pass:android --v1-signing-enabled true --v2-signing-enabled true --out signed.apk aligned.apk
6. Verify: "$BT/apksigner" verify --verbose signed.apk  (expect v1=true, v2=true).

=== DEVICE / "WHEN TO PLUG IN THE PHONE" ===
Validate on the arm64 emulator FIRST (API 36 defaults to 4KB pages, so the 4KB-aligned lib loads):
  - Start server (docker) listening 0.0.0.0:9960 with client_host=127.0.0.1:9960.
  - adb uninstall sg.gumi.bravefrontier   (new self-signed key != original)
  - adb install signed.apk
  - adb reverse tcp:9960 tcp:9960
  - Launch; confirm it reaches http://127.0.0.1:9960/bf/gme/action.php (server TRACE log / http_log) and login completes.
Only after the emulator run confirms login + main screen, PLUG IN THE PHYSICAL PHONE and repeat: adb uninstall, adb install signed.apk, adb reverse tcp:9960 tcp:9960, launch.
